records.claimSummary: Clients batch events and send them every 10 seconds
records.conditionSummary: or sooner when the app goes to the background
records.mustConvey: sent sooner than 10 s when the app goes to the background
records.bindingReason: When the app is backgrounded, events are not sent on the 10-second cadence, so 'every 10 seconds' alone is misleading.

records.claimSummary: Each event carries an account id
records.conditionSummary: account id only for signed-in users
records.mustConvey: account id only for signed-in users
records.bindingReason: Events from anonymous users carry no account id, so the unscoped claim is false for them.

records.claimSummary: Clients send event types (to the collector)
records.conditionSummary: every event type must be registered before clients can send it
records.bindingReason: An unregistered event type cannot be sent (and is rejected), so 'clients send events' is false for it.
records.notes: Intra-sentence; overlaps with u8 rejection rule, which u2_n4 also carries.

records.claimSummary: The enrichment step adds account attributes (plan tier, region) to events
records.conditionSummary: if the account cannot be found, the event is passed on without account attributes
records.mustConvey: account not found -> passed on without attributes
records.bindingReason: For events whose account is not found, no attributes are added, so 'adds account attributes' is false for them.

records.claimSummary: Events reach the warehouse in real time, so launch dashboards stay current
records.conditionSummary: enriched events are written to the warehouse in hourly batches (contradicts real time)
records.bindingReason: With hourly batch loads, data can be up to an hour old, so 'real time' is false as written.
records.notes: The central ambiguity of the source. g5 is a top-level frame whose takeaway repeats the real-time claim; its only arrow is g0->g5. u2_a1 says 'batch loading' but not hourly, so not counted as carrier. No node flags the contradiction.

records.claimSummary: The enrichment step uses the user service
records.conditionSummary: user service expected to stay lightly loaded, so enrichment should avoid adding much traffic
records.mustConvey: enrichment must not add much traffic to the user service
records.bindingReason: Enrichment still uses the user service; the load limit adds a design constraint rather than falsifying the claim.
records.notes: u2_n11 is joined to the shape u2_n7 ('constraint' arrow), not to u2_n8; both hang off u2_n7 but no direct arrow. Source wording is itself ambiguous (lightly loaded as expectation vs. requirement).

records.claimSummary: Raw events are kept for 30 days and then deleted
records.conditionSummary: the components table lists warehouse raw events retention as 90 days (contradicts 30)
records.bindingReason: If warehouse raw events are kept 90 days per the table, the 30-day statement is false or at least contested.
records.notes: Conflicting retention values between prose and table. The table node carries 90 days but nothing flags the conflict; g6 is linked only to g1, not g2. u7_n2 ('fixed period') not counted as a claim card as it states no value.

records.claimSummary: Only aggregated tables are kept longer than 30 days
records.conditionSummary: how long aggregated tables are kept is TBD
records.bindingReason: The claim that aggregated tables outlive raw events stays true; the open retention period is a caveat to note somewhere.
records.notes: Same frame, no arrow; g6 takeaway doesn't mention TBD.

records.conditionSummary: once the mobile SDK is ready; no date set
records.mustConvey: depends on mobile SDK being ready; no date
records.bindingReason: Mobile events are not added until the SDK is ready, so an unconditioned 'phase 2 adds mobile events' implies a commitment that doesn't exist.
records.notes: u9_n4 is also linked to u9_n5; frame g8 takeaway 'mobile pending SDK' conveys it.

records.claimSummary: Approval is requested to start phase 1 (open questions settled in parallel)
records.conditionSummary: the cost of running the pipeline has not been estimated
records.bindingReason: The approval request stands as stated; the missing cost estimate is a caveat a decision-maker must see somewhere.
records.notes: Whether the cost caveat is a condition on the approval ask is a judgement call. g9 is joined to g8 (a carrier via its takeaway) by the g8->g9 arrow.

records.claimSummary: A change requires a new schema version rather than an edit
records.conditionSummary: only breaking changes require a new version
records.bindingReason: For non-breaking changes the new-version rule does not apply, so dropping 'breaking' overstates it.

notes: Two source-internal contradictions (r5 real time vs hourly batches; r7 30 vs 90 days) are recorded as deciding facts; the notes reproduce both sides but never connect them. No records for examples (plan tier/region, first dashboards), open questions (u39-u41, which restate u18/u8), non-goals (u27/u28, scope statements carried verbatim by u8_n1/u8_n2), privacy rules (u25/u26) or the phase-1 estimate (u37, carried in u9_n2). u20 (launch reviews within 2 hours) not recorded separately: it is the requirement the r5 contradiction bears on.
